page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.6xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based virtual machine configured for high-frequency compute and high-throughput networking. The instance runs on an Intel Xeon 8252C processor operating at 4.5 GHz across 24 dedicated vCPUs (12 physical cores with two threads per core) built on the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is 96.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, relying on network-attached Amazon EBS for persistent disks, and includes no dedicated hardware GPUs. Network connectivity provides a 50 Gbps baseline interface with zero bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reflect a balance of high single-core frequency and robust memory subsystem performance. PassMark memory testing ranks in the top 25% with a score of 2910.35, while single-threaded gzip compression achieves 31.99 GB/sec, also placing in the top quartile. General computing benchmarks show solid middle-tier results, such as a PassMark CPU score of 27739.41, a Geekbench multi-core score of 11058.0, and a stress-ng multi-core rate of 28955.19. In-memory caching and throughput testing demonstrate 25.7 million Redis SET operations per second and 17.36 GB/sec in static web serving. For lightweight language models (135M), inference reaches 1184.96 prompt tokens per second, but heavy processing falls sharply without GPU acceleration, managing only 4.06 tokens per second on a 70B model.

From an efficiency perspective, the m5zn.6xlarge balances high sustained clock speeds against standard general-purpose memory allocations, delivering strong per-core execution without the overhead of extreme memory overheads. Tradeoffs center on the absence of bundled local NVMe storage and lack of accelerators, which limits native database caching speeds and large-scale AI generation compared to specialized storage or GPU instances. The m5zn.6xlarge is appropriate for high-throughput web serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters, and compute-intensive enterprise application workloads requiring 50 Gbps network bandwidth.
description: Amazon Web Services m5zn.6xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance designed for compute-bound applications that require high network bandwidth and high CPU frequency. Powered by a 24-vCPU Intel Xeon 8252C processor running at 4.5 GHz across 12 physical cores, it includes 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory at 3 GHz, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 50 Gbps baseline networking, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and omits local storage and hardware GPUs, utilizing remote EBS volumes for storage. Benchmark results show strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression (31.99 GB/sec) and PassMark memory testing (2910.35), alongside steady multi-core execution across Geekbench and stress-ng suites. Delivering balanced memory density alongside elevated clock frequencies, the m5zn.6xlarge is well-suited for Redis in-memory data structures, software build pipelines, high-traffic web applications, and network-intensive backend services.
